text.tspan: the envelope of the audio that is used to calculate gain reduction
is created by analog components. then that envelope is read into
a ADC on the STM32, and digitally, the gain reduction is calculated
from the audio dyanmic envelope and the user's attack, release,
threshold and ratio settings. then, that gain reduction is turned
into a control voltage and sent back to analog with a DAC on the
STM32, and that gain reduction / compression is actually applied
in analog with VCAs. (this is a vca compressor with a hybrid
G = -40...+20 dB (cut and make-up), 0 dB = 1.308 V
COMP_CV = 0.2685 - 0.2053 x GR_DAC (DAC FS 2.048 V, 6.1 mV/dB)
DAC 0 V (reset, R11) = -44 dB: a failure always cuts, never boosts.
ENV_ADC = 0.221 x |DET_IN|: +22 dBu sine = 3.05 V peak, -30 dBu = 9.5 LSB peak.
R6/C2: 3.4 kHz anti-alias for fs >= 20 kHz. Peak/RMS, attack and release in firmware.
